title: Linked List Intersection Node
statement:
Find where two acyclic singly linked lists first share storage.

Contract
- `first` and `second` may be null. Both reachable lists are acyclic.
- Nodes are the same only when they are the exact same object; equal values do not count as an intersection.
- Return the first shared node encountered while walking from each head, or null when the two lists are disjoint.
- Do not mutate either list.

Examples
- Lists `1 -> 2 -> 8 -> 9` and `3 -> 8 -> 9` that share the `8` node return that `8` node.
- Lists `1 -> 2` and `1 -> 2` built from separate nodes return null.
- If both heads are the same object, return that head.

examples.input: both heads are the same node

hints: First compare list lengths so both walkers can be the same distance from the tail.
Advance the longer list walker by the length difference.
Move both walkers together until they are identical or both reach null. Intended complexity: O(a + b) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: shared tail, first prefix, second prefix separated by semicolons, for example: [8, 9]; [1, 2]; [3]
